# divizu

> A deterministic DSL → SVG renderer for architecture diagrams that coding agents can write.

divizu gives a coding agent a tiny language for expressing a repository's
architecture as a drawing with real sockets, plugs and modules. The user gets a
clean SVG instead of a wall of prose. The renderer has zero runtime
dependencies, needs no browser, and produces byte-identical output for the same
DSL.

## Start here

- Agent skill: https://jeysef.github.io/divizu/skills/divizu.md
- Playground: https://jeysef.github.io/divizu/playground.html
- Reference manual: https://jeysef.github.io/divizu/docs.html
- Quickstart source: https://jeysef.github.io/divizu/examples/quickstart.di
- Quickstart output: https://jeysef.github.io/divizu/examples/quickstart.svg
- Large system map (28 blocks): https://jeysef.github.io/divizu/examples/large.di

## Use it

Ask the agent:

> Use divizu to diagram this project's architecture. Read
> https://jeysef.github.io/divizu/skills/divizu.md and follow it. Write the
> architecture as a `.di` file, render it to SVG, and show me the result.

Fastest delivery without installing anything: URL-encode the DSL and return a
playground link.

```text
https://jeysef.github.io/divizu/playground.html#dsl=<encodeURIComponent(dsl)>
```

To render a file:

```bash
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/Jeysef/divizu
cd divizu
npm install
npm run build
node dist/cli.js architecture.di -o architecture.svg
```

## DSL

```dsl
CheckoutApi "composition root" {
  role: root
  socket Orders <- OrderService
  socket Telemetry
  socket Config <- AppConfig
}

OrderService "application service" {
  role: composite
  modules: ValidateCart, PriceOrder
  socket Payments <- StripeAdapter
}

StripeAdapter { role: adapter }

AppConfig "context" { role: context }
```

```dsl
BlockId ["subtitle"] {
  role: root | composite | service | adapter | port | layer | context
  modules: name, "name, with comma", name
  candidates: Name, Name(RequiredInterface), Name
  socket PortName
  socket PortName <- ProviderBlockId
}
```

The layout reads bottom-up: the root sits at the bottom, sockets open upward,
and implementations sit above them. Use unbound sockets for dependencies outside
the diagram. Keep diagrams to roughly 5–25 blocks and split large systems by
bounded context.

## Properties

- Input: plain-text `.di` DSL.
- Output: deterministic, self-contained SVG.
- Runtime: zero dependencies, no DOM, no canvas, no headless browser.
- Validation: duplicate ids, dangling providers, unreachable blocks and cycles
  fail with readable errors.
- License: MIT.
